t: There's nothing to see here now, but this spot is where Goose-Pie House once stood. It was a small English Baroque house built in 1701 by John Vanbrugh, and it was demolished in 1898. The site now lies under the southeast corner of the Old War Office Building on Whitehall, near the Gurkha Memorial statue on Horse Guards Avenue. Vanbrugh is best known as the designer of Blenheim Palace and Castle Howard. He was also a dramatist, and his comedies The Relapse and The Provoked Wife are still staged today.
